evals.prompt: Draft the PR title and description for my already-pushed `fix/session-expiry-231` branch against `main`; do not create it yet. The change fixes sessions that remained valid after a password reset because the verifier compared only token expiry and ignored `credentialsChangedAt`. The diff adds that timestamp check and regression tests. `npm test -- session-verifier` passed. This fully fixes issue #231. Keep it concise and don't mention what tool wrote the code.
evals.expected_output: A compact, provider-neutral PR draft with an outcome-oriented title, a fenced Markdown body, a short summary/root-cause explanation, the actual validation command, and `Closes #231` because the supplied context says the default-branch PR fully resolves it.
expectations: The title describes the session invalidation fix rather than implementation mechanics or authorship.
The PR body is wrapped exactly once in a fenced `markdown` block in the conversational response.
The body is concise and includes only material summary or root-cause context plus the observed validation.
The body uses `Closes #231` or an equivalent valid closing keyword for the explicitly supplied, fully resolved issue.
The output contains no claim that an agent, model, provider, or tool authored the change.

evals.prompt: Write a PR for the pushed `settings-mobile-layout` branch. It changes the account settings modal so the actions stack below 640px and the destructive action stays separated. Tests: `pnpm test SettingsModal` passed, and I verified 390x844 and 1440x900 in the browser. Use these uploaded images in the body: before `https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/before-123`, after `https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/after-456`. I did not give you an issue and I don't want you hunting for one. Return the title and Markdown draft only.
evals.expected_output: A concise fenced PR description with summary, actual validation, and a focused visual-evidence section using the supplied URLs with useful labels. It should omit issue linkage and avoid searching for or inventing an issue.
expectations: The body uses both supplied GitHub attachment URLs and distinguishes before from after with useful alt text or captions.
The body records the two verified viewports and the passed test without inventing additional validation.
No issue section, issue number, or suggestion to search the issue tracker appears.
The description remains compact and does not add empty risk, rollout, migration, or checklist sections.
The output uses a single fenced `markdown` block and contains no agent or provider attribution.

evals.prompt: Update the description for existing draft PR #88. The branch changes checkout retry behavior: after a recoverable card-network timeout, the Retry button preserves the cart and returns to payment instead of restarting checkout. `pnpm test checkout-retry` and the Playwright retry flow passed. I recorded `artifacts/checkout-retry.webm`, but it has not been uploaded anywhere. This is behavioral and I want a short demo in the PR. Do not pretend the local path works on GitHub, and do not mark the PR ready.
evals.expected_output: A concise draft-PR update with summary and validation plus a demo placeholder or media-pending note. It must not fabricate a GitHub URL or embed the local path as if remote, should keep the PR in draft, and should report the exact local artifact that still needs authorized upload.
expectations: The body explains the observable retry behavior rather than narrating file changes.
The body includes only the two supplied passing validations.
The output does not use `artifacts/checkout-retry.webm` as a Markdown link or claim the video is already attached.
The result keeps PR #88 as a draft and identifies authorized upload of the local video as the remaining action.
The body is shown in exactly one fenced `markdown` block and contains no agent, model, or provider attribution.

evals.prompt: Draft a title and body for my unpushed branch. The complete diff retries the request once on HTTP 503 and adds a passing test for that case. Leave the commits alone. No issue.
evals.expected_output: A local PR text draft for the stated change.
expectations: Returns a title and body without requiring a remote head.
Uses the supplied test evidence, with no invented command or issue.
Does not publish or rewrite commits.

evals.prompt: Use $pr-authoring. Make this PR easy to review: I have 9 noisy WIP commits (`wip`, `fix typo`, `oops`). Propose a dependency-ordered commit reorganization plan and show how you will prove the git tree did not change.
evals.expected_output: Groups actual dependent commits, records the original tree, and explains how to verify content equivalence.
expectations: Proposes a commit reorganization plan before rewriting history or force-pushing.
Bases groups on the actual dependencies in the change.
Records `ORIGINAL_TREE` before history rewrite and verifies `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` equality afterward.
Refuses to push if the tree hash changed unintentionally.

evals.prompt: Use $pr-authoring. Make PR #77 easier to review without rewriting git history—just improve the PR description and reviewer guidance.
evals.expected_output: Leaves commit history untouched and updates reviewer guidance with an accurate TL;DR, core vs mechanical file separation, risk/migration callouts, and verification notes.
expectations: Does not rewrite commit history when the user asks to keep history untouched.
Separates core logic files from generated or mechanical files in the reviewer guide.
Adds a truthful TL;DR, risky change callouts, and test coverage notes.

evals.prompt: This 4,500-line PR touches three unrelated subsystems. Use pr-authoring to advise how to handle it.
evals.expected_output: Identifies that the PR mixes unrelated changes and is too large for notes alone, and recommends splitting into focused PRs rather than polishing around the problem.
expectations: Flags mixed unrelated changes and excessive diff size.
Recommends splitting the PR rather than masking the scope with prose notes alone.
Never hides behavior changes inside history cleanup.

evals.prompt: Our branch is local and unpushed. It contains three commits: add schema, implement export, and test export. Prepare a short reviewer guide from these supplied facts only; no publication, no history changes, no tools.
evals.expected_output: Provides a local reviewer guide without requiring a push or creating a PR.
expectations: Does not require the local branch to be pushed before preparing the guide.
Preserves history and does not claim publication.
Uses only the supplied schema, export and test scope.
